programs.name: IncreasingBST.java
programs.description:
Increasing Order Search Tree
 
Given the root of a binary search tree, rearrange the tree in in-order so that the leftmost node in 
the tree is now the root of the tree, and every node has no left child and only one right child.
 Example 1:
          5                     1
         / \                     \
        3   6          --->    2
       /\   /\                     \
      2  4    8                    3
     /       / \                     \
     1       7  9                    4
                                        \
                                         5
                                          \
                                           6
                                            \
                                             7
                                              \
                                               8
                                                \
                                                 9


Input: root = [5,3,6,2,4,null,8,1,null,null,null,7,9]
Output: [1,null,2,null,3,null,4,null,5,null,6,null,7,null,8,null,9]

Example 2:
         5            1
        /\     --->  \
       1  7             5
                           \
                            7
Input: root = [5,1,7]
Output: [1,null,5,null,7]


Approach:
1.It defines a global variable newRoot of type TreeNode which will store 
   the current node in the rearranged tree.
2.The increasingBST method calls a helper method DFS 
   (which stands for Depth First Search) with the root of the input tree.
3.The DFS method recursively traverses the tree in a specific order 
   (right, root, left) known as "reverse in-order traversal".
4.During the traversal, it sets the newRoot variable to point to 
   the current node, effectively building the skewed binary tree in the 
   desired order.

programs.name: ActivitySelection.java
programs.description:
The Activity Selection Problem is an optimization problem which deals with the selection of non-conflicting activities that needs to be executed by a single person or machine in a given time frame.

Each activity is marked by a start and finish time.
Let's consider that you have n activities with their start and finish times, the objective is to find solution set having maximum number of non-conflicting activities that can be executed in a single time frame, assuming that only one person or machine is available for execution.

Some points to note here:

It might not be possible to complete all the activities, since their timings can collapse.
Two activities, say i and j, are said to be non-conflicting if si >= fj or sj >= fi where si and sj denote the starting time of activities i and j respectively, and fi and fj refer to the finishing time of the activities i and j respectively.
Greedy approach can be used to find the solution since we want to maximize the count of activities that can be executed. This approach will greedily choose an activity with earliest finish time at every step, thus yielding an optimal solution.

Input Data for the Algorithm:
act[] array containing all the activities.
s[] array containing the starting time of all the activities.
f[] array containing the finishing time of all the activities.

Ouput Data from the Algorithm:
sol[] array refering to the solution set containing the maximum number of non-conflicting activities.


Steps for Activity Selection Problem
Following are the steps we will be following to solve the activity selection problem,

Step 1: Sort the given activities in ascending order according to their finishing time.

Step 2: Select the first activity from sorted array act[] and add it to sol[] array.

Step 3: Repeat steps 4 and 5 for the remaining activities in act[].

Step 4: If the start time of the currently selected activity is greater than or equal to the finish time of previously selected activity, then add it to the sol[] array.

Step 5: Select the next activity in act[] array.

Step 6: Print the sol[] array.

The sentence is circular.

- eetcode's last character is equal to eetcode's first character.
The sentence is circular.

{
    public static int rob(int[] nums) 
	{
        int n = nums.length;
        int[] memo = new int[n];
        Arrays.fill(memo, -1); // initialize memo array with -1
        return compute(nums, n - 1, memo);
    }

    public static int compute(int[] nums, int i, int[] memo)
	{
        if (i < 0) return 0;
        if (memo[i] != -1) return memo[i];

        int rob = nums[i] + compute(nums, i - 2, memo); // choose to rob current
        int skip = compute(nums, i - 1, memo);          // skip current
        memo[i] = Math.max(rob, skip);                 // take the best option

        return memo[i];
    }

courses prerequisites. 
The minimumSemesters method takes in an integer maxCourses that represents the
maximum number of courses that can be
taken in a semester and returns the minimum number of semesters needed to complete 
all courses.

The method performs topological sort by creating an adjacency list representation of the 
graph using the prerequisites array, calculating the indegrees of all the vertices, initializing
a queue with vertices that have indegree 0, and processing vertices in the queue while 
updating the indegrees of their adjacent vertices. The method keeps track of the number

programs.code:
import java.util.*;

public class ParallelCourses {
    private int V; // number of courses
    private int[][] prerequisites; // array of prerequisite courses

    public ParallelCourses(int V, int[][] prerequisites) {
        this.V = V;
        this.prerequisites = prerequisites;
    }

    public int minimumSemesters(int maxCourses) {
        // create an adjacency list to represent the graph
        List<Integer>[] graph = new List[V];
        for (int i = 0; i < V; i++) {
            graph[i] = new ArrayList<>();
        }

        // populate the adjacency list using the prerequisites array
        for (int[] edge : prerequisites) {
            graph[edge[1]].add(edge[0]);
        }

        // perform topological sort
        int[] indegree = new int[V];
        for (int i = 0; i < V; i++) {
            for (int j : graph[i]) {
                indegree[j]++;
            }
        }

        Queue<Integer> queue = new LinkedList<>();
        for (int i = 0; i < V; i++) {
            if (indegree[i] == 0) {
                queue.add(i);
            }
        }

        int semesters = 0;
        int coursesTaken = 0;
        while (!queue.isEmpty()) {
            int coursesThisSemester = Math.min(queue.size(), maxCourses);
            for (int i = 0; i < coursesThisSemester; i++) {
                int u = queue.poll();
                coursesTaken++;
                for (int v : graph[u]) {
                    indegree[v]--;
                    if (indegree[v] == 0) {
                        queue.add(v);
                    }
                }
            }
            semesters++;
        }

        if (coursesTaken != V) {
            return -1; // cannot complete all courses
        }

        return semesters;
    }
	public static void main(String[] args) 
	{
		int numCourses = 6;
        int[][] prerequisites = {{1,0},{2,0},{3,1},{3,2},{4,3},{5,4}};

        ParallelCourses p=new ParallelCourses(numCourses, prerequisites);

        System.out.println(p.minimumSemesters(2)); 
	}
}
